subtopic: Expert parallelism and sequence parallelism / Purposes and dataflow
learningObjective: Distinguish expert parallelism (EP) and sequence parallelism (SP) from TP/PP and identify their communication primitives.
stem: Which comparison of Expert Parallelism (EP) and Sequence Parallelism (SP) is correct?

options.text: EP places different experts of a Mixture-of-Experts on different devices; token-to-expert routing requires all-to-all communication to shuffle tokens to their assigned expert. SP shards intermediate activations along the sequence dimension inside a TP region (e.g., after a norm) to reduce activation memory; SP requires AllGather/ReduceScatter around the sharded region.
EP shards attention heads across experts; SP shards the sequence length across attention groups. Both are Attention-only parallelism schemes and do not touch the MLP block.

Both EP and SP shard the MLP weights across devices. They differ only in whether the shard axis is aligned with expert index (EP) or with sequence position (SP); both require a single AllReduce per MLP block just like TP.
EP is used for training-time load balancing only and has no role in inference; SP is exclusively an inference-time trick that reduces KV cache footprint by sharding along the sequence axis.

explanation: EP (Expert Parallelism, from GShard / DeepSpeed-MoE / vLLM MoE): experts of a MoE layer are placed on different devices; routing shuffles tokens to their assigned expert via all-to-all, and results are all-to-all'd back. SP (Sequence Parallelism, from Megatron): inside a TP region, some ops (norm, dropout) that don't need cross-hidden-dim communication are sharded along the sequence axis instead of being replicated; AllGather/ReduceScatter transitions between SP and TP regions save activation memory. They serve different purposes and have different communication patterns.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: EP = MoE expert placement + all-to-all; SP = sequence-axis sharding within TP region.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: EP is about experts (MLP), not attention heads; SP is not attention-only.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: both are collapsed into an incorrect single collective.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: EP is heavily used in inference; SP is not about KV cache.

assumptions: Standard EP as in GShard / DeepSpeed-MoE / vLLM MoE.
SP is defined as in Megatron-LM's sequence-parallel augmentation of TP.
nonImplications: Does not imply EP and TP cannot be combined; they often are (e.g., TP=8 within a node, EP across nodes).
Does not imply SP is universally beneficial; small models may not need it.

performanceClaim.scope: EP and SP definitions and communication patterns
